.method public static parse(Ljava/lang/String;)I
    .registers 3

    const-method-handle v0, invoke-static@Ljava/lang/Integer;->parseInt(Ljava/lang/String;)I
    invoke-polymorphic {v0, p0}, Ljava/lang/invoke/MethodHandle;->invokeExact([Ljava/lang/Object;)Ljava/lang/Object;, (Ljava/lang/String;)I
    move-result v0
    return v0
.end method

.method public static intToString()Ljava/lang/invoke/MethodType;
    .registers 1

    const-method-type v0, (I)Ljava/lang/String;
    return-object v0
.end method

sections.title: Roughly equivalent Java
invoke-polymorphic and invoke-custom
sections.body:
invoke-polymorphic (format 45cc, or 4rcc for /range) calls a signature-polymorphic method such as MethodHandle.invokeExact. It carries two references: the declared method, whose generic ([Ljava/lang/Object;)Ljava/lang/Object; signature is fixed, and a separate prototype that describes the real argument and return types at this call site. The result, if any, is read with the usual move-result* instruction.

invoke-custom (35c, or 3rc for /range) resolves a call site the first time it executes: the runtime calls the bootstrap method named in the call site item, which must return a CallSite, and then invokes that CallSite's target with the instruction's arguments. It is the DEX counterpart of the JVM's invokedynamic.

sections.title: A desugared capturing lambda
sections.body:
.method public static schedule(Ljava/util/concurrent/Executor;Ljava/lang/String;)V
    .registers 3

    new-instance v0, Lcom/acme/demo/Jobs$$ExternalSyntheticLambda0;
    invoke-direct {v0, p1}, Lcom/acme/demo/Jobs$$ExternalSyntheticLambda0;-><init>(Ljava/lang/String;)V
    invoke-interface {p0, v0}, Ljava/util/concurrent/Executor;->execute(Ljava/lang/Runnable;)V
    return-void
.end method

sections.title: Lambdas and string concatenation
sections.body:
javac compiles a lambda to an invokedynamic that bootstraps through LambdaMetafactory. D8 does not pass that through: it desugars lambdas and method references on every API level. Each lambda becomes a synthetic class named like Jobs$$ExternalSyntheticLambda0 that implements the functional interface, stores captured values in fields set by its constructor, and forwards the interface method to a synthetic method holding the lambda body (typically lambda$schedule$0 in the original class). Non-capturing lambdas are usually shared through a static instance instead of being allocated at every use.

String concatenation is similar. javac 9+ emits an invokedynamic to StringConcatFactory.makeConcatWithConstants; D8 normally rewrites it into a StringBuilder chain, so that is what app DEX files usually contain. A raw call site looks like this:

sections.title: An invoke-custom call site (not desugared)
Desugaring in practice
sections.body:
Other desugarings you will meet in Smali:
- Default and static interface methods with minSdk below 24 are moved into a companion class named like Shape$-CC and called with invoke-static.
- try-with-resources works on all API levels; D8 rewrites the Throwable.addSuppressed call it relies on where the platform lacks it.
- Core library desugaring (coreLibraryDesugaring in Gradle) rewrites references to newer Java APIs such as java.time into a bundled copy whose package starts with j$, e.g. Lj$/time/LocalDate;.
- MethodHandle.invoke and invokeExact cannot be desugared, so code that uses them needs minSdk 26.

exercises.prompt: Write a static method stringLength()Ljava/lang/invoke/MethodHandle; that returns a method handle for the instance method String.length() using const-method-handle.
exercises.starterCode:
.method public static stringLength()Ljava/lang/invoke/MethodHandle;
    .registers 1
    # load the handle into v0 and return it
.end method
exercises.solution:
.method public static stringLength()Ljava/lang/invoke/MethodHandle;
    .registers 1
    const-method-handle v0, invoke-instance@Ljava/lang/String;->length()I
    return-object v0
.end method
exercises.hint: The handle kind for a virtual method is written invoke-instance@ followed by the method reference. const-method-handle needs DEX 039 (API 28).

exercises.prompt: The invoke-custom version of label(String, int) above cannot run below API 26. Rewrite it with StringBuilder so it works on any API level, producing the same text ("<name> = <value>").
exercises.hint: Each \u0001 in the recipe is one dynamic argument and the rest is constant text. Use the append(I) overload for the int.

exercises.prompt: In the schedule() example, where does the body of the lambda actually live, and how does the Executor end up running it?
exercises.solution:
The body is a synthetic method in Jobs itself (for example a static lambda$schedule$0 that
takes the captured String). Jobs$$ExternalSyntheticLambda0 implements Runnable, keeps the
captured String in a field set by its constructor, and its run() method calls the synthetic
method with that field. The Executor only ever sees a Runnable and calls run().
exercises.hint: Look for a class implementing Runnable and a synthetic method whose name starts with lambda$.

quiz.question: Which DEX version (and Android release) introduced const-method-handle?
quiz.explanation: DEX 038 (API 26) added invoke-polymorphic and invoke-custom; DEX 039 (API 28) added const-method-handle and const-method-type.

quiz.question: What is special about invoke-polymorphic compared with invoke-virtual?
options: It carries an extra prototype reference describing the call site's actual types
It can only call static methods
It uses 16-bit register fields for all arguments
quiz.explanation: Format 45cc stores both a method reference (e.g. MethodHandle.invokeExact) and a proto reference with the real argument and return types used at this call site.

quiz.question: You see this in an app built with D8. What produced it?
options: A desugared lambda or method reference
An anonymous inner class written in Java source
quiz.explanation: D8 desugars lambdas into synthetic classes named Outer$$ExternalSyntheticLambdaN. Anonymous classes written in source keep names like Outer$1.

quiz.question: With minSdk 21, where does D8 put the body of a static method declared in an interface Shape?
options: In a companion class such as Shape$-CC, called with invoke-static
It stays in Shape and is called with invoke-interface
It is inlined everywhere and removed
It is rejected; static interface methods need minSdk 26
quiz.explanation: Before API 24 the runtime cannot run code in interfaces, so D8 moves static and default method bodies into a $-CC companion class and rewrites the call sites.

quiz.question: How is the result of an invoke-custom call read?
options: With a move-result* instruction immediately after it
From the CallSite object returned by the bootstrap method
It is always written to v0
quiz.explanation: Like every invoke, invoke-custom leaves its result in the hidden result slot; the next instruction must be the matching move-result, move-result-wide or move-result-object.

lessons.title: Reading Obfuscated Smali
lessons.summary: Release builds processed by R8 have short renamed identifiers, inlined and merged code, and synthetic helper classes. Learn what each transformation looks like in Smali and a systematic way to make sense of your own minified builds, using mapping.txt when you have it.

sections.title: Scope
sections.body: This lesson is about understanding builds you own or are explicitly authorised to analyse: your own release APKs, crash triage for your team's app, or an audit you were contracted to do. Do not use these techniques to defeat licensing, authentication, payments or other protections, and respect the terms and laws that apply to you.

sections.title: What R8 changes
sections.body:
R8 shrinks, optimises and obfuscates. Obfuscation renames classes, fields and methods that are not protected by keep rules to short names such as a, b, c or aa, and can move classes into short or flattened packages. Some names always survive:
- entry points the system must find by name (components declared in the manifest, classes kept for reflection or serialization),
- everything outside your app: framework and library types such as Landroid/app/Activity; or Ljava/lang/String; and the methods you call on them.

Those surviving names are your anchors.

sections.title: A minified class
The same class, renamed by hand
Optimisations and synthetic code
sections.body:
Optimisation changes the shape of the code, not just the names:
- Inlining: small methods and getters disappear into their callers.
- Class merging: a class can be merged into its only subclass or with similar classes.
- Enum unboxing: simple enums may become plain ints.
- Debug info: .local entries are removed and the source file is often reported as "SourceFile"; .line entries remain only so stack traces can be mapped back.
- Register reuse: as above, a parameter register like p1 can be overwritten once it is dead.

Synthetic members and classes also appear: access$000-style static accessors that older javac versions generated for private members used by nested classes (newer D8 versions produce names containing -$$Nest$ when desugaring nest-based access), $$ExternalSyntheticLambdaN classes for lambdas, and $$ExternalSyntheticOutlineN classes holding instruction sequences that R8 outlined into shared static methods to save space.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body:
A workable routine:
- Start from anchors: const-string literals, framework calls (getBoolean, startActivity, Log), and manifest components.
- Follow types: field and parameter types tell you what a renamed class holds.
- Rename as you go and keep notes; meaning builds up across classes.
- For your own builds, use the mapping file R8 writes (by default app/build/outputs/mapping/release/mapping.txt) and the retrace tool to turn obfuscated stack traces back into real names. Archive the mapping for every release you ship.

exercises.prompt: Describe what this method from your own release build does and propose meaningful names for the class, the field and the method.
exercises.solution:
It reads a Context stored in field c, asks it for the package name and returns
"build: " + packageName. Reasonable names: field c -> context, method b() -> buildLabel(), and
class La/b/d; -> something like AppInfo or BuildInfoProvider, depending on its other members.
exercises.hint: The framework calls (Context.getPackageName, String.concat) and the string literal are never renamed.

exercises.prompt: Your crash report shows a frame in a.b.c.a(String). The mapping.txt from that release contains the lines below. What is the real method?
exercises.starterCode:
com.acme.demo.flags.FeatureFlags -> a.b.c:
    android.content.SharedPreferences prefs -> a
    boolean isEnabled(java.lang.String) -> a
exercises.solution:
a.b.c is com.acme.demo.flags.FeatureFlags, and its method a taking a String is
boolean isEnabled(String). The field a in the same class is prefs. Running retrace with this
mapping file over the full stack trace does this translation automatically.
exercises.hint: Each class line maps original -> obfuscated; the indented lines below it are its members.

quiz.question: Which names does R8 never rename in your app's DEX?
options: Framework and library classes you call, such as Landroid/content/SharedPreferences;
Every class in the default package
quiz.explanation: R8 can only rename code it is processing. References to the Android framework and other platform classes must keep their real names, which makes them reliable anchors.

quiz.question: What does a class named Lcom/acme/demo/a$$ExternalSyntheticOutline0; usually contain?
options: Shared static methods holding instruction sequences R8 outlined to save space
quiz.explanation: Outlining extracts repeated code sequences into a static helper so each caller can replace them with one invoke-static.

quiz.question: Is writing the result into p1 here valid?
quiz.code:
.method public final a(Ljava/lang/String;)Z
    .registers 4
    iget-object v0, p0, La/b/c;->a:Landroid/content/SharedPreferences;
    const/4 v1, 0x0
    invoke-interface {v0, p1, v1}, Landroid/content/SharedPreferences;->getBoolean(Ljava/lang/String;Z)Z
    move-result p1
    return p1
.end method
options: Yes; p1 is an ordinary register and is no longer needed after the call
No; move-result can only target v-registers
quiz.explanation: Parameter registers are normal frame registers. Once the argument is dead the allocator may reuse its register, which minified code does often.

quiz.question: What are access$000-style static methods?
options: Synthetic accessors older javac versions generated so nested classes could reach private members
Methods R8 created by merging classes
quiz.explanation: Before Java 11 nestmates, a nested class could not access its outer class's private members directly, so javac generated package-visible static accessors named access$NNN.

quiz.question: How do you translate an obfuscated stack trace from your own release build?
options: Run retrace with the mapping.txt R8 produced for that exact build
Rebuild the app and compare method names
Use any mapping.txt from a recent build
quiz.explanation: Names are assigned per build, so only that build's mapping file is correct. Keep it with every release you ship.

lessons.title: Debugging & Validation
lessons.summary: Make edited Smali trustworthy: what the debug directives mean, how to round-trip code through baksmali and smali, how to read assembler errors and VerifyError messages, and how to use the Playground diagnostics in this app before anything reaches a device.

sections.title: Debug directives
sections.body:
Debug directives come from the DEX debug_info_item and have no effect on what the code computes:
- .line N maps the following instructions to source line N (used in stack traces and debuggers).
- .param pN, "name" names a parameter.
- .local vN, "name":Type starts a local variable's range in vN; .end local vN ends it; and .restart local vN reopens a variable that was ended earlier, for example after a branch.
- .prologue and .epilogue mark where the method's setup ends and its exit code begins; you rarely see them in modern output.

Deleting them keeps the code working but loses line numbers and variable names.

sections.title: A method with line information
sections.body:
.method public static clamp(III)I
    .registers 3
    .param p0, "value"    # I
    .param p1, "min"    # I
    .param p2, "max"    # I

    .line 12
    if-ge p0, p1, :cond_3
    .line 13
    return p1

    .line 15
    :cond_3
    if-le p0, p2, :cond_6
    .line 16
    return p2

    .line 18
    :cond_6
    return p0
.end method

sections.title: Round trips and assembler errors
sections.body:
A round trip is the simplest validation: disassemble with `baksmali d classes.dex -o out`, edit, then reassemble with `smali a out -o classes.dex` (apktool does the same for whole APKs with `apktool d` and `apktool b`). The result is functionally equivalent, not byte-identical:
string and type ordering, payload placement and debug info encoding may differ.

The assembler catches syntax and encoding problems: an unknown mnemonic, a missing .end method, an undefined label, a literal that does not fit (const/4 accepts only -8 to 7), a register outside the range of a 4-bit format, or a method with no instructions. It does not check types or data flow; that is the verifier's job.

sections.title: What the verifier rejects
Assembles, but fails verification (uninitialised reference)
Use the Playground diagnostics
sections.body: Validate in small steps: write a method in the Playground, read the diagnostics panel (it lists errors and warnings with line numbers), fix the first error before the rest because later ones are often consequences, and only then round-trip the whole class. On a test device, filter logcat for VerifyError to see the exact offset the verifier complained about.

exercises.prompt: This method assembles but is rejected by the verifier. Find the problem and fix it.
exercises.hint: new-instance only allocates. What must run before any other method is called on the object?

exercises.prompt: The assembler rejects this method with "Invalid literal value: 16. Must be between -8 and 7, inclusive." Fix it so it returns 16.
exercises.starterCode:
.method public static sixteen()I
    .registers 1
    const/4 v0, 0x10
    return v0
.end method
exercises.solution:
.method public static sixteen()I
    .registers 1
    const/16 v0, 0x10
    return v0
.end method
exercises.hint: const/4 holds a signed 4-bit literal. Pick the next larger const form.

exercises.prompt: This method assembles, but the verifier reports that execution can fall off the end of the code. Fix it so it returns the absolute value of p0.
exercises.starterCode:
.method public static abs(I)I
    .registers 1
    if-gez p0, :done
    neg-int p0, p0
    :done
.end method
exercises.solution:
.method public static abs(I)I
    .registers 1
    if-gez p0, :done
    neg-int p0, p0
    :done
    return p0
.end method
exercises.hint: Every path through a method must end in a return, a throw or a jump back into the code.

quiz.question: What happens at runtime if you delete every .line directive from a method?
options: The code behaves the same, but stack traces lose line numbers
quiz.explanation: .line entries only populate debug info. They map instructions to source lines for stack traces and debuggers and never change what the code does.

quiz.question: This code assembles. What happens when the class is loaded?
options: The verifier rejects it: the StringBuilder is used before <init> runs
It runs and returns an empty string
Nothing; uninitialised objects are allowed for StringBuilder
quiz.explanation: new-instance produces an uninitialised reference. The only legal use is calling a constructor on it; anything else is a hard verification failure (VerifyError).

quiz.question: The assembler says "Invalid register: v17. Must be between v0 and v15, inclusive." on an iget line. What fixes it?
options: Copy the value into a low register first, e.g. with move-object/from16
quiz.explanation: iget uses format 22c with 4-bit register fields. Move the value to v0-v15 first; adding registers would only push the parameters higher.

quiz.question: Which statement about a baksmali then smali round trip is true?
options: The new DEX is functionally equivalent but not necessarily byte-identical
It always produces a byte-identical file
quiz.explanation: The assembler may order and encode items differently. It also does no type checking, so a successful round trip does not prove the code will verify.

quiz.question: What does `.end local v3` tell you?
options: The named variable in v3 goes out of scope; v3 may be reused afterwards
v3 must not be written again in this method
v3 is the last register of the frame
quiz.explanation: It closes the debug range of the variable. The register itself is free for the allocator to reuse, often for a different variable.

flashcards.front: What are the 8 magic bytes of a version 039 dex file?
flashcards.back: The bytes 64 65 78 0a 30 33 39 00, i.e. "dex\n039\0". The three digits are the format version.

flashcards.front: How large is the dex header?
flashcards.back: 0x70 (112) bytes for versions up to 040. The experimental 041 container format uses 0x78 bytes.

flashcards.front: checksum vs signature in the dex header?
flashcards.back: checksum: Adler-32 of everything after the checksum field. signature: 20-byte SHA-1 of everything after the signature field.

flashcards.front: What are the fields of a method_id_item?
flashcards.back: class_idx (ushort, type_ids), proto_idx (ushort, proto_ids) and name_idx (uint, string_ids): 8 bytes.

flashcards.front: What is the map_list?
flashcards.back: A table of contents in the data section, at header.map_off. Each 12-byte entry gives an item type, a count and an offset, ordered by offset.

flashcards.front: What do the characters in a format id like 22c mean?
flashcards.back: First digit: code units. Second digit: max registers (r = range). Letter: extra data (c = pool index, t = branch target, s/i/l/n/b = literals, x = none).

flashcards.front: How is format 35c laid out?
flashcards.back: A|G|op BBBB F|E|D|C: A = argument count, B = reference index, C..G = up to five 4-bit argument registers.

flashcards.front: Encode const/4 v0, 1.
flashcards.back: Format 11n (B|A|op): B = 1, A = 0, op = 0x12, so the unit is 0x1012, stored as the bytes 12 10.

flashcards.front: Which goto can have a zero offset?
flashcards.back: goto/32. goto and goto/16 must not use offset 0; a spin loop needs goto/32 or a nop as the target.

flashcards.front: How many code units do switch payloads use?
flashcards.back: packed-switch-payload: size * 2 + 4. sparse-switch-payload: size * 4 + 2. Both must be 4-byte aligned.

flashcards.front: What does invoke-polymorphic carry besides the method?
flashcards.back: A proto@HHHH reference with the call-site prototype. It calls signature-polymorphic methods such as MethodHandle.invokeExact (dex 038, API 26).

flashcards.front: How is an invoke-custom call site linked?
flashcards.back: On first execution the bootstrap method from call_site_item runs and returns a CallSite; its target handle is then invoked. Bootstrap failures throw BootstrapMethodError.

flashcards.front: What are the three .annotation visibilities?
flashcards.back: build (tools only, like RetentionPolicy.CLASS), runtime (reflection, like RUNTIME) and system (dalvik.annotation.* metadata for the runtime).

flashcards.front: What is a shorty descriptor?
flashcards.back: The compact prototype string in proto_id_item: return type first, then one character per parameter, with every reference type written as L. (Ljava/lang/String;I[J)Z becomes ZLIL.

flashcards.front: A method has .registers N and K parameter words. Which v-register is p0?
flashcards.back: v(N - K). Parameters occupy the last K registers, with `this` first for instance methods.

flashcards.front: Why do compiled methods contain move-object/from16 shuffles?
flashcards.back: Formats such as 12x, 22c, 22t and 35c encode registers in 4 bits (v0-v15). Values in higher registers must be copied down first.
flashcards.code:
move-object/from16 v0, p0
iget-object v1, v0, Lcom/acme/demo/User;->name:Ljava/lang/String;

flashcards.front: What register widths does format 22x (move/from16) use?
flashcards.back: An 8-bit destination vAA and a 16-bit source vBBBB.

flashcards.front: Which DEX version added invoke-polymorphic and invoke-custom?
flashcards.back: Version 038, supported from Android 8.0 (API 26).

flashcards.front: Which DEX version added const-method-handle and const-method-type?
flashcards.back: Version 039, supported from Android 9 (API 28).

flashcards.front: What two references does invoke-polymorphic carry?
flashcards.back: A method reference (e.g. MethodHandle.invokeExact) and a proto reference with the call site's actual argument and return types. Format 45cc, or 4rcc for /range.

flashcards.front: Load the method type (I)Ljava/lang/String; into v0.
flashcards.back: Use const-method-type (format 21c, API 28+).

flashcards.front: What is a class named Outer$$ExternalSyntheticLambda0?
flashcards.back: A synthetic class D8 generated when desugaring a lambda or method reference. It implements the functional interface and forwards to the lambda body in Outer.

flashcards.front: What is a Shape$-CC class?
flashcards.back: A D8 companion class holding static and default interface method bodies when minSdk is below 24.

flashcards.front: What does the descriptor Lj$/time/LocalDate; indicate?
flashcards.back: Core library desugaring: references to java.time were rewritten to the bundled j$ copy for older API levels.

flashcards.front: What do .local and .end local mark?
flashcards.back: The start and end of a named source variable's range in a register. Debug info only; no runtime effect.
flashcards.code:
const/4 v0, 0x0
.local v0, "count":I
add-int/lit8 v0, v0, 0x1
.end local v0    # "count":I

flashcards.front: What does .line N do?
flashcards.back: Maps the following instructions to source line N for stack traces and debuggers. It does not change execution.

flashcards.front: When is java.lang.VerifyError thrown?
flashcards.back: When a class whose code fails hard verification is loaded, e.g. register type mismatches, using an object before <init>, or code that can fall off the end.

flashcards.front: Where does R8 write the mapping file for a release build, and what reads it?
flashcards.back: By default app/build/outputs/mapping/release/mapping.txt; the retrace tool uses it to deobfuscate stack traces.

flashcards.front: What does the .super directive declare?
flashcards.back: The direct superclass of the class, written as a type descriptor, e.g. .super Ljava/lang/Object;

flashcards.front: What does move-result-object do?
flashcards.back: Copies the object reference returned by the immediately preceding invoke-* (or filled-new-array) into a register.

flashcards.front: Which on-device tool compiles DEX bytecode ahead of time in ART?
flashcards.back: dex2oat. It reads DEX files and writes OAT files containing native code, guided by a compilation filter such as speed-profile.

flashcards.front: In which Android release did ART fully replace Dalvik?
flashcards.back: Android 5.0 (Lollipop). Android 4.4 offered ART only as a developer option.

flashcards.front: What hybrid execution model did Android 7.0 introduce?
flashcards.back: Interpretation plus a JIT that records hot methods in a profile, followed by profile-guided AOT compilation by dex2oat when the device is idle and charging.

flashcards.front: What are the 8 magic bytes at the start of a DEX file?
flashcards.back: The text dex, a newline, a three-digit version and a zero byte, e.g. dex\n039\0.

flashcards.front: What does the 64K limit of a DEX file refer to?
flashcards.back: A single DEX file can reference at most 65,536 methods (16-bit index), counting library and framework methods as well. Fields and types have the same limit.

flashcards.front: How are additional DEX files in a multidex APK named?
flashcards.back: classes.dex, then classes2.dex, classes3.dex and so on. apktool disassembles classesN.dex into smali_classesN/.

flashcards.front: How large is a Dalvik code unit?
flashcards.back: 16 bits. Instructions are 1 to 5 code units long, and branch offsets are counted in code units.

flashcards.front: Is Dalvik bytecode stack-based or register-based?
flashcards.back: Register-based. Each method declares a fixed set of virtual registers and instructions name them explicitly, unlike the JVM's operand stack.

flashcards.front: How does a class declare that it implements an interface?
flashcards.back: With one .implements line per interface, placed after .super.

flashcards.front: What does .source record?
flashcards.back: The name of the original source file (e.g. "User.java"), used in stack traces. It is optional and has no effect on behaviour.

flashcards.front: What is the descriptor of the nested class Entry inside com.acme.demo.Cache?
flashcards.back: Lcom/acme/demo/Cache$Entry; — nested and anonymous classes are joined to the outer name with $.

flashcards.front: How does an interface look on the .class line?
flashcards.back: The flags abstract and interface appear together, because DEX stores both for interfaces.

flashcards.front: Which DEX version introduced invoke-polymorphic and invoke-custom?
flashcards.back: Version 038, supported from Android 8.0. Version 039 (Android 9) added const-method-handle and const-method-type.

flashcards.front: Where do a method's parameters live in its register frame?
flashcards.back: In the last registers of the frame. With N registers and P parameter registers, pX is v(N - P + X).

flashcards.front: What does p0 hold in an instance method?
flashcards.back: this, the object the method was called on. Declared parameters start at p1.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between .registers and .locals?
flashcards.back: .registers N is the total register count including parameters. .locals N counts only non-parameter registers; the assembler adds the parameter registers.

flashcards.front: How are long and double values stored in registers?
flashcards.back: In a pair of consecutive registers, always referred to by the lower number (e.g. v0 means v0 and v1).

flashcards.front: Which descriptor letters stand for boolean and long?
flashcards.back: Z is boolean and J is long. B (byte) and L (class prefix) were already taken.

flashcards.front: What Java type is [[I?
flashcards.back: int[][], a two-dimensional int array.

flashcards.front: How is the nested class java.util.Map.Entry written as a descriptor?
flashcards.back: Ljava/util/Map$Entry; using the binary name with $ between outer and inner class.

flashcards.front: What literal range does const/4 accept?
flashcards.back: A signed 4-bit value from -8 to 7, and the destination must be v0 to v15.

flashcards.front: What does const/high16 do?
flashcards.back: Loads a 16-bit literal into the top half of a 32-bit register and clears the bottom half. Common for float constants such as 1.0f.

flashcards.front: When is const-string/jumbo used?
flashcards.back: When the string's index in the DEX string table does not fit in 16 bits (above 65535).

flashcards.front: Which registers can format 12x instructions such as move or add-int/2addr address?
flashcards.back: Only v0 to v15, because both register fields are 4 bits wide.

flashcards.front: What is a shorty descriptor?
flashcards.back: The compact form of a prototype stored in proto_ids: return type first, then parameters, with every reference or array type written as L. (ILjava/lang/String;[J)Z becomes ZILL.

flashcards.front: What are a constructor and a static initialiser called in Smali?
flashcards.back: Instance constructors are <init> and the static initialiser is <clinit>; both carry the constructor flag.
flashcards.code:
.method public constructor <init>()V
    .registers 1
    invoke-direct {p0}, Ljava/lang/Object;-><init>()V
    return-void
.end method

flashcards.front: Which methods have no register directive and no instructions?
flashcards.back: abstract and native methods: their .method line is followed directly by .end method.

flashcards.front: Which methods are called with invoke-direct?
flashcards.back: Non-overridable instance methods: private methods and constructors (<init>), including the superclass constructor call.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between formats 35c and 3rc for invokes?
flashcards.back: 35c lists up to five 4-bit argument registers individually. 3rc (the /range forms) takes a contiguous block {vN .. vM} of up to 255 registers with 16-bit register numbers.

flashcards.front: What does move-result-wide do?
flashcards.back: Copies a long or double return value of the immediately preceding invoke into a register pair (vAA and vAA+1).

flashcards.front: How many argument registers does a long parameter use in an invoke?
flashcards.back: Two: a long or double occupies a register pair, and both registers are listed in the braces.

flashcards.front: What can filled-new-array not create?
flashcards.back: Arrays of long or double: the elements must be single-word values. int arrays and reference arrays are allowed. The result must be fetched with move-result-object.

flashcards.front: What does the number after .array-data mean?
flashcards.back: The element width in bytes (1, 2, 4 or 8) for the fill-array-data payload that follows.

flashcards.front: Which instruction reads an element of a float[] array?
flashcards.back: Plain aget. There is no aget-float; aget and aput handle all 32-bit primitive elements such as int and float.

flashcards.front: What do cmpl-float and cmpg-float return for NaN?
flashcards.back: cmpl-* (lt bias) returns -1 and cmpg-* (gt bias) returns 1. Compilers use cmpg for < and <=, cmpl for > and >=.

flashcards.front: Why can if-eqz use v200 but if-eq cannot?
flashcards.back: if-testz uses format 21t with an 8-bit register. if-test uses format 22t, which packs two 4-bit registers into one byte, so both registers must be v0-v15.

flashcards.front: What does if-eqz test when the register holds a reference?
flashcards.back: Whether the reference is null. if-nez jumps when it is not null.

flashcards.front: What are the parts of a field reference such as Lcom/acme/demo/A;->count:I?
flashcards.back: The defining class descriptor, ->, the field name, a colon and the field type descriptor.

flashcards.front: Which formats do iget and sget use?
flashcards.back: iget/iput use 22c (two 4-bit registers plus a field index); sget/sput use 21c (one 8-bit register plus a field index).

flashcards.front: When does aput-object throw ArrayStoreException?
flashcards.back: When the stored value's runtime type is not assignable to the array's actual element type.

flashcards.front: What does rsub-int/lit8 v0, v1, 0x5 compute?
flashcards.back: v0 = 5 - v1. The rsub (reverse subtract) instructions subtract the register from the literal. rsub-int is the 16-bit literal form.

flashcards.front: Which arithmetic instructions throw ArithmeticException?
flashcards.back: Integer division and remainder (div-int, rem-int, div-long, rem-long and their /2addr and literal forms) when the divisor is zero. Float and double division never throw.

flashcards.front: What is the format of add-int/2addr and what does it compute?
flashcards.back: Format 12x: two 4-bit registers. add-int/2addr vA, vB computes vA = vA + vB, so only v0 to v15 can be used.

flashcards.front: How do the /lit8 and /lit16 binop forms differ?
flashcards.back: /lit8 is format 22b: 8-bit registers and a signed 8-bit literal. /lit16 is format 22s: 4-bit registers and a signed 16-bit literal. Only /lit8 has shift variants.

flashcards.front: Which registers does add-long v0, v2, v4 use?
flashcards.back: It writes the pair v0/v1 and reads the pairs v2/v3 and v4/v5. Wide values are named by their lower register.

flashcards.front: How many bits of the shift distance do shl-int and shl-long use?
flashcards.back: shl-int, shr-int and ushr-int use the low 5 bits (distance & 0x1f); the long versions use the low 6 bits. The long shifts take the distance from a single int register.

flashcards.front: What does float-to-int do with NaN and huge values?
flashcards.back: It rounds toward zero, converts NaN to 0, and clamps values that are too large to 0x7fffffff or -0x80000000.

flashcards.front: What must happen after new-instance before the object is used?
flashcards.back: A constructor (<init>) must be called on it with invoke-direct. Until then the reference is uninitialised and the verifier rejects other uses.

flashcards.front: check-cast versus instance-of?
flashcards.back: instance-of vA, vB, type stores 1 or 0 (null gives 0). check-cast vAA, type throws ClassCastException on failure and lets null pass; afterwards the register has the checked type.

flashcards.front: Where is move-exception allowed?
flashcards.back: Only as the first instruction of an exception handler. It stores the caught exception in an 8-bit register.

flashcards.front: What is the syntax of a typed catch handler in smali?
flashcards.back: List the exception type, the covered label range and the handler label.

flashcards.front: When do compilers emit .catchall?
flashcards.back: For finally blocks (cleanup copied into a handler that rethrows) and synchronized blocks (the handler runs monitor-exit before rethrowing).

flashcards.front: What happens if a method declared to return J uses return instead of return-wide?
flashcards.back: The assembler accepts it, but the verifier rejects the method when the class is loaded, raising VerifyError.

flashcards.front: Which return instruction does a method returning boolean use?
flashcards.back: Plain return vAA. Booleans, bytes, chars, shorts, ints and floats are all 32-bit values; return-wide is for long/double and return-object for references.
